text:
marta: Heads up — after last night's node image + nvdriver 525.60 bump, a subset of A100s in us-west1 show missing MIG slices and kube pods are stuck Pending. Noticing device minors shifted.

raj: link to alerts: https://ops/alerts/3245 :eyes: Which nodes?

marta: us-west1-a, a few in b. Canary nodes 10-12. I saw nvml reports show different 'gpu_instance_id' mapping.

jin: can you paste nvml query? run: 
```sh
nvidia-smi mig -lgci
nvidia-smi -q -x | grep -A5 MIG
```

marta: pasted: 
```text
GPU 0: MIG profiles: none (expected 7g.40gb)
GPU 0 UUID: GPU-abcdef123456 -> but nvml lists device minor 13 for the same profile
```

nina: kubelet logs show device plugin re-registering and then complaining 'mismatched device id'

ops-oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-213 (MIG capacity mismatch us-west1). Priority P2.

raj: Are we sure it's the driver not kernel? We also rolled kernel livepatch 5.17.9 last night.

jin: Checked: nvidia-drv 525.60.2 vs previous 525.60.0 — NVML ABI bump included according to release notes. Could be device enumeration reorder.

marta: Rolling back driver on two canaries now.

marta: kubectl drain node-usw1-canary-10 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

nina: Pods drained. After rollback, MIG profiles came back on those nodes. Looks promising.

raj: @vendor-support-bot opened a case with NVIDIA; gave logs. They asked for /var/log/nvidia/* and nvidia-smi -q output.

vendor-support-bot: Case NV-78932 opened. Assigned to eng-sup. ETA 24h.

jin: Plan: halt fleet-wide nvdriver rollouts. Patch release notes in infra-runbook. We'll coordinate kernel reverts too.

marta: Note: some nodes show 'nvhost' binding error in dmesg: `nvhost: failed to attach mig instance to device`

nina: Workaround: restart nvidia-hostengine? `systemctl restart nvidia-hostengine` temporarily rebinds but not reliable.

raj: Cost note: affected nodes were autoscaled hosts serving high-cost inference workloads. If we leave them down we'll route to other regions. Notify SRE and PG.

marta: I've opened a support ticket for customers on Dedicated capacity impacted. Messaging drafted.

jin: Next steps: 1) rollback driver on remaining canaries 2) freeze driver rollouts 3) run a small playbook to check nvml/gpu_instance_id mapping 4) schedule fleet maintenance window to coordinate kernel+driver together.

nina: :thumbsup: Will prepare the playbook and a nightly job to scan for mismatched MIG counts and stash results in S3.

marta: Adding note to incident: potential NVML ABI incompatibility causing MIG device-id remapping; search for 'gpu_instance_id' mismatch.

raj: If vendor says it's expected behavior maybe we need to implement a node-level migration step: drain -> remove MIG configs -> install driver -> reapply MIG profiles -> reboot.

ops-oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-213 updated: status=investigating assignees=[marta, jin]

marta: Thanks team. I'll post a short postmortem template after RCA.
